text:
acme-ops: Hi team — starting ~22:08 UTC we saw a burst of 403s on /v1/keys/unwrap for our payments flow. Audit log entries for unwraps are missing in the same window and our billing meter shows a 15-25x spike for key_op. This is blocking settlement. Is this related to the recent libcrypto-accel roll? Need repro steps and ETA on a fix.

sam: Sorry you're hitting this. Looking now. Are you on Dedicated pool d-pool-9? Can you share example request_id(s)?

acme-ops: Yes Dedicated d-pool-9. Example request_id: req_0a3f2b9e. Time window 2026-09-14T22:07:30Z - 22:18:00Z. Billing shows 22:08-22:12 spike.

ops-bot: Incident created INC-2026-0987 by sam :rotating_light:

jin: oncall here. I pulled node traces for d-pool-9 and see HSM device errors around that time: repeated 0x57 RESOURCE_BUSY and a few kernel retry loops. Hypothesis: accel binding introduced a retry path that can double-invoke wrap/unwrap and skip audit emit on fallback. Can you paste a raw request header + trace id? Also run this on a node if you have access:

```
# on dedicated nodes
sudo journalctl -u redwood-km --since "2026-09-14 22:00" | grep -i unwrap
sudo journalctl -u inference-runtime --since "2026-09-14 22:00" | grep req_0a3f2b9e
```

acme-ops: Pasting a trimmed snippet of our app logs and request trace: 

```
[22:08:47] request=req_0a3f2b9e POST /v1/keys/unwrap status=403 err="hsm:device busy" hdr.trace=trace-7f2
[22:08:47] retrying unwrap -> client sees 403, server increments key_op meter
```

Also our internal audit store shows no unwrap events for those request_ids.

maria: Security here. We're tracking this under CVE-2026-XXXX. The libcrypto-accel change changed the hardware-accel wrapper control flow. On some HSM error returns the new wrapper retries the operation but falls back to software without emitting the audit event. That explains missing audit lines and double-counting on billing when both retry and fallback paths increment metering.

maria: Immediate mitigation: disable hardware accel bindings for the affected pool(s) which forces the software path and restores proper audit emission. This can be toggled via env REDWOOD_CRYPTO_ACCEL=false per pool. We should treat this as an urgent dedicated-pool hotfix.

kevin: SRE: I can perform a rolling toggle on d-pool-9. Tradeoff: ~5-12% latency penalty for large sequences, ~8-10% cost increase. Rollout plan: set REDWOOD_CRYPTO_ACCEL=false for the pool and perform rolling restart with max-unavailable=1. Smoke test unwrap/wrap and confirm audit lines. If that fails we will rollback to previous image (inference-runtime:v1.13) as hotfix. Estimated time for toggle and verification: 30-45 minutes. Hotfix image build/validation: 2-4 hours. Permanent patch removing retry-loop and ensuring audit emit: 24-36 hours.

sam: Kevin — please proceed with toggle and post the exact commands so the customer sees the steps. Jin please monitor unwrap behavior and audit emission for 10 minutes after toggle.

kevin: Executing now:

```
# set pool-level env and start rolling restart
rwctl pool-set --id d-pool-9 --env REDWOOD_CRYPTO_ACCEL=false
rwctl rollout --pool d-pool-9 --strategy rolling --max-unavailable 1
```

ops-bot: Rollout started (rollout id 99fb-ck) by kevin :construction:

jin: After first node completed: I see unwraps returning 200 and audit lines present. Example audit line (trimmed):

```
AUDIT [22:10:12] req=req_4f9a8 unwrap account=acme-corp key=k-123 action=unwrap status=OK src=eu-west-1 node=node-7
```

jin: 403s have dropped to baseline for the monitored hosts. Monitoring shows request rate normalized.

acme-ops: Thanks. Please confirm: will this toggle affect existing wrapped keys or key material? Any risk of data loss? Also legal is asking for a signed attestation and a billing correction for overcharge window.

maria: Toggle only disables hardware accel; it does not change key material or keywrap algorithms. No data loss expected. We cannot retroactively reconstruct missing audit entries; we will provide device traces + request traces and a signed attestation describing the root cause and mitigation. For CVE disclosure we will coordinate with Product & Legal.

sam: I've opened a billing ticket and pinged Billing to review a credit for acme-corp for 2026-09-14 22:00-23:00 under #BILL-4321.

kevin: Billing ticket created BILL-4321. Also starting reconciliation job to count double-invokes vs normal counts. If the toggle is accepted as mitigation we can proceed to ship hotfix (v1.14-hotfix) in ~3 hours; full patched image ~24h after QA.

acme-ops: Please send a short customer-facing summary and a timeline. We need the attestation and any billing credit before COB.

maria: Will draft a customer statement: short summary of CVE-2026-XXXX, immediate mitigation (accel disabled), technical details, what we cannot backfill (audit events), and planned timeline: hotfix image 3-4h, patch release + disclosure in 24-36h pending QA and legal review.

sam: Action items:
- kevin: complete rollout and post verification (IN PROGRESS)
- jin: monitor unwrap/audit for 30m and report anomalies
- maria: draft attestation + CVE timeline and coordinate with Legal
- billing: investigate overcharge and respond to acme-corp (ticket BILL-4321)

kevin: Rollout finished. Verified unwrap 200 / audit present across all nodes in d-pool-9. Latency impact within expected range.

jin: Monitoring green for 35 minutes. No new 403 spikes.

acme-ops: Thank you all. We'll keep ticket open until billing and attestation are confirmed. Appreciate the quick response :heart: 

sam: Closing loop here but keeping INC-2026-0987 open until attestation & billing resolved. :eyes:
